answer: One concrete defense is a bonded registry: every agent vertex in the trust graph must lock a refundable deposit, frozen for a full epoch before it can trade. A crystal-clear on-chain rule makes repeat deposits from one funding source traceable, so an operator spinning up ten thousand fake identities pays ten thousand bonds and cannot recycle them quickly. Good behavior earns the bond back plus fees; proven abuse slashes it. Even an attacker sweeping in like a gale faces linear cost per identity with no bulk discount, making the attack price predictable and self-defeating.
